title: Vacuum sealing w/o a machine BUT it takes a lot of stamina to remove the air & it’s not perfect
text:
Vacuum sealing w/o a machine BUT it takes a lot of stamina to remove the air & it’s not perfect. I have mixed feelings about this vacuum sealing option. On one hand I wish I had known about this before I purchased my Foodsaver Vacuum Sealer, but on the other hand, I am glad I have that machine even though it is quirky.

For the current price of $25.29, the following items are included in the box:
- 1 hand pump
- 10 extra large vacuum bags (11.8" x 13.4")
- 10 large vacuum bags (10.2" x 13.4")
- 10 medium vacuum bags (10.2" x 11")
- 4 sous vide holding clips (used to clip the bag to the side of the sous vide)
- 2 bag sealing clips (the white clips used to seal the zipper)

The only instructions are on the box. I inserted the food into the bag and pressed out most of the air by hand. I then used the white sealing clip to seal the zipper. I had to try this three times before I was successful. What I found is that it is best to place the bag flush with the counter and then press down hard on the white sealing clip as one slides it across the bag top.

Once the bag was sealed, I placed the pump over the "hole" to suck out the air. I also had trouble with this. I had to push down hard on the pump to create a suction with the "hole" in the bag that is not really a hole. Then it took immense effort to pump the pump up and down. I felt like I was inflating a bicycle tire manually. I really had trouble with the effort this took.

Once I was done, I removed the pump, clipped the bag to the sous vide, and started the cooking process. The bag floated a little bit after awhile. This means that air does seep back into the bag. However, I have had this with my machined sealed items as well. Lucky the clips keep the food submerged.

Cleaning out the bag is not easy. I know I had a hard time because I was unable to clean out the corners even when turning the bag inside out. I wound up throwing it out. I am skeptical of re-using them because they cannot be fully cleaned; especially with fish, meat, or something marinated. The Amazon site says each bag can be re-used more than 10 times; I seriously doubt that nor would I count on that. I would consider one use to be typical. For me, it has been one use only.

In summary, this is one option to try if a machine vacuum sealer is not available. I do think this is a viable option for those who use a sous vide intermittently. However, if someone uses a sous vide regularly, I would not recommend this due to the difficulty and price of replacement bags -- since washing them out is difficult to impossible.
